summary: In Greek mythology, Argus (Argos) son of Arestor is the shipwright who, with Athena's guidance, built the fifty-oared Argo for Jason's quest of the Golden Fleece. Apollonius Rhodius has Athena teach him at Pagasae and fit a speaking oak from Dodona in the prow. Distinct from Argus Panoptes, Odysseus's dog Argos, Colchian Argus son of Phrixus, and other Argus/Argos figures.
attribution: Adapted from Wikipedia, "Argo" and "Argus (mythology)" · CC BY-SA 4.0
etymology: The ship Argo is usually named after her builder Argus; some ancients derived Ἀργώ from a word for "swift" instead. The personal name Ἄργος shares the "bright / nimble" root of other Argos figures.

sections.heading: Building the Argo
paragraphs: Apollonius makes Argus son of Arestor Athena's pupil in constructing the vessel in Thessaly near Pelion / Pagasae. Apollodorus describes a fifty-oared ship — a mythic penteconter — whose crew the Argonauts themselves supplied. A sacred Dodona oak in the prow spoke oracles; Hera protected the voyage.

Hyginus also knows an Argive Argus (son of Polybus and Argia, or of Danaus) as builder; traditions vary on whether the shipwright sailed with the crew. The ship was later dedicated to Poseidon at the Isthmus of Corinth.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: Ancient and modern writers sometimes conflate the Arestorid shipwright with Argus son of Phrixus and Chalciope at Colchis (atlas id argus-colchis). The atlas keeps them apart: argus-arestor is the builder; argus-panoptes the hundred-eyed watchman; argos-dog Odysseus's hound.
